data.title: Bulten Subsidiary Exim Wins Strategic Lam Research Supply Deal in Asia
data.description:

Bulten AB’s wholly owned subsidiary Exim has secured a strategic agreement to act as consolidator for C-parts supply to Lam Research’s semiconductor equipment manufacturing operations in Malaysia, Taiwan and South Korea. By leveraging its sourcing capabilities, supplier network and logistics expertise, Exim aims to meet complex supply chain needs and support Lam Research’s expansion in Asia, aligning itself with robust demand drivers such as digitalization, artificial intelligence and data center investment.

data.title: Gix Invests $500,000 in Ottonomy to Expand Physical AI and L4 Robotics Strategy
data.description:
Gix ( (IL:GIXI) ) has shared an announcement.

On September 15, 2026, Gix Internet Ltd. announced it had signed a $500,000 simple agreement for future equity (SAFE) to make a strategic investment in Ottonomy Inc., a U.S.-based Physical AI robotics firm developing Level 4 autonomous robotic systems. The SAFE gives Gix contractual rights to receive equity in Ottonomy upon future qualifying financing or other specified events, with closing of the investment expected in the week of September 16, 2026, subject to customary conditions.

The move deepens Gix’s push to build a single intelligent management layer for robots, people and autonomous systems, leveraging Deliverz.ai’s hospital logistics platform alongside Ottonomy’s Ottobot autonomous delivery robots, which are deployed and piloted across hospitals, airports, industrial sites and last-mile environments for major healthcare and pharmaceutical clients. A non-binding letter of intent signed on August 4, 2026, contemplates potential additional investments that could eventually give Gix a strategic or even majority stake in Ottonomy, signaling an effort to broaden its autonomous operations footprint and strengthen its positioning in Physical AI and robotics across healthcare, industrial and logistics markets.

data.title: BrenX Strikes EIB Debt Settlement to Halve Liabilities and Bolster Equity
data.description:
The latest update is out from BrenX ( (BRNX) ).

On September 15, 2026, BrenX announced a settlement agreement with the European Investment Bank that will cancel its March 2021 credit facility, eliminate approximately $4.8 million of related debt and release associated security following an initial €1.1 million payment and satisfaction of closing conditions. Management’s illustrative estimates suggest the transaction could cut total liabilities by about 54%, lift shareholders’ equity by roughly 77% and generate around $3.6 million in income, marking a significant strengthening of BrenX’s balance sheet and supporting its shift from a manufacturing‑focused TES model toward an integrated industrial energy platform.

The settlement closes a financing chapter that helped BrenX build what it describes as the world’s first gigafactory dedicated to heat battery production, moving bGen™ systems from development into commercial‑scale manufacturing. By removing scheduled principal and interest obligations to the EIB and easing collateral constraints, the agreement is expected to provide greater near‑term financial flexibility as BrenX pursues long‑term, infrastructure‑style energy solutions for industrial clients, though an additional €2.9 million payment would be triggered if specified qualifying transactions occur within one year of the initial settlement payment.

data.title: China Water Industry Faces Liquidation as Hong Kong Sets Strict Path to Trading Resumption
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from China Water Industry Group Limited ( (HK:1129) ).

China Water Industry Group Limited, now in liquidation, operates across sewage treatment and construction, renewable energy, property investment and development, and waste management and recycling, giving it exposure to essential infrastructure and environmental services in regulated markets. Its multi-segment structure ties performance to long-term projects whose viability depends heavily on corporate stability and continued access to financing and public markets.

The company has had joint liquidators formally appointed by the Hong Kong High Court, and trading in its shares remains suspended while it works to address delayed publication of its 2026 interim results and report. The Hong Kong Stock Exchange has set out resumption guidance requiring the company to clear all outstanding financial reporting, resolve the winding-up order and discharge liquidators, demonstrate compliance with listing rules, and fully inform the market, underscoring the significant uncertainty facing shareholders and creditors over future operations and listing status.

data.title: Coya Therapeutics Advances COYA 302 ALS Phase 2/3 Trial
data.description:
The latest announcement is out from Coya Therapeutics, Inc. ( (COYA) ).

On September 15, 2026, Coya Therapeutics reported that the one hundredth patient has been enrolled in its ongoing Phase 2/3 ALSTARS Trial of COYA 302 for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The randomized, multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled study aims to enroll 120 participants, with current trends supporting completion in time to report topline data in early Q2 2027.

The trial is structured with a 24-week double-blind treatment phase followed by a 24-week blinded active-treatment extension, giving up to 48 weeks of data on COYA 302. Its primary endpoint is change in disease severity measured by ALSFRS-R from baseline to Week 24 versus placebo, with additional objectives focused on efficacy, safety, tolerability, biological activity, and biomarker assessments, underscoring Coya’s push to advance its ALS program.
